introduction: On this fifth Sunday of Easter, Paul and Barnabas strengthen the new Christian communities and report how God has opened the door of faith to the nations. John sees a new heaven and a new earth, and God says, Behold, I make all things new. In the Gospel, Jesus gives his disciples a new commandment: love one another as I have loved you. Let us be known as his disciples by our love.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord is good to all and compassionate to all his creatures. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that all people may recognize Christ's disciples by their love for one another. Let us pray to the Lord.
For Christians who face hardship for their faith: that they may persevere, knowing that through many trials we enter the Kingdom of God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who mourn and those in pain: that God may wipe away every tear from their eyes. Let us pray to the Lord.
For divided families and communities: that the new commandment of love may heal them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may love one another as Jesus has loved us. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God of love, you make all things new in your risen Son. Teach us to love one another as he loved us, and bring us to the new Jerusalem. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: A new commandment
reflection.body:
The Gospel takes us back to the Last Supper. Judas has just gone out into the night to betray Jesus. At that very moment, Jesus speaks of glory: "Now the Son of Man has been glorified." His glory will be revealed on the cross, in a love that gives everything.

Then he speaks tenderly to his disciples: "Little children, I will be with you a little while longer." Before he leaves, he gives them a new commandment: "that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also love one another." The commandment to love was not new. What is new is the measure: as I have loved you. And he gives them a sign by which the world will recognize them: "By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another."

The first reading shows the early Church living this love. Paul and Barnabas go back to the communities they founded, "strengthening the souls of the disciples," and telling them honestly "that through many afflictions we must enter into God's Kingdom." Then they return home and tell how God "had opened a door of faith to the nations."

The Book of Revelation gives us a vision of where this love leads: "a new heaven and a new earth." God himself will live among his people: "He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain any more." And God says, "Behold, I am making all things new."

The new world begins wherever Christians love one another as Christ loved them. This week, look at the people closest to you, at home, at work or in your parish. Choose one concrete way to love one of them as Jesus would.
